must_identify.item: Only one of the two frontend pods fails (502/504, it cannot connect to its upstream), the other serves normally
must_identify.evidence: `rr7xl`, which started before the bad edit, continued running a working configuration and successfully proxied to the backend, while `r4thz`, which came up after the ConfigMap was changed, mounted the broken config and returned repeated `504 Gateway Timeout` errors on every `/api/items` request due to upstream connection timeouts to `10.96.137.47:8000`

must_identify.item: The cause is the frontend-nginx ConfigMap upstream changed to api:8000; only the restarted pod has loaded it, the other still runs the old config
must_identify.evidence: The root cause was a misconfigured `frontend-nginx` ConfigMap that pointed nginx's `/api/` upstream at port 8000, while the live `api` Service actually listens on port 8080 [16, 21, 19]. Because nginx only reads this config at container startup and does not hot-reload, the two frontend replicas diverged

notes: The RCA recommends no fix at all, so it does not say to revert the ConfigMap to api:8080 before restarting. It also does not warn that restarting rr7xl would break it too. It calls the alert high-severity when it was a warning, which is a minor inaccuracy.
